findings.description: Slippage minOut is computed on the FULL pre-buffer aggregate (`totalShares`) and the entire surplus is sold in a single swap, but the recipient only receives the post-buffer remainder (`underlyingReceived - totalSetAside`). Any caller-side floor (e.g. SYA's `minRewardTokenSupplied`) that the keeper enforces against the externally returned `underlyingReceived` is the SWAP output — not the recipient's actual receipt. A caller wiring its slippage floor to the function's return value is effectively unprotected against value diverted into per-client buffers, because the swap's own minOut never accounts for the buffer split. Author NatSpec acknowledges this tradeoff (lines 246–251 of AYieldStrategy.sol).
missingMitigations: No floor on `toRecipient` itself (only on the unbuffered swap output)
Caller-side slippage floor (e.g. minRewardTokenSupplied) must be applied to the function's documented return value, not to the swap result — relies on integrator discipline
Aggregate buffer percentage is not capped, so all-clients-at-100% reduces recipient to zero with no revert
references: CLAUDE.md note: skimSurplus return value vs SurplusSkimmed events
findings.notes: This is the user-highlighted concern. The leak is bounded by the buffer percentages (which only redirect funds between protocol-owned contracts), but a future client that the protocol does not directly own — or a buggy integrator that treats skimSurplus's return as ground-truth without subtracting buffers — could mis-account. Forward to econ-scanner for full impact analysis; the buffer redirection is documented as 'protocol-internal', so the most realistic angle is an integrator API contract / accounting drift, not a direct theft path.

findings.description: Every swap's minOut is derived from `vault.convertToShares` / `vault.convertToAssets` — i.e., the external ERC4626 vault's REPORTED share price — and scaled by `slippageToleranceBps`. Since the AMM swap actually executes against an AMM pool (e.g. Curve), this anchor only protects against the *vault's* reported price diverging from the AMM clearing price by more than `slippageToleranceBps`. The pattern matches: spot price (from the ERC4626 vault) used as slippage benchmark for an AMM execution.
matchedSignatures: uint256 idealShares = vault.convertToShares(amount); uint256 minOut = idealShares * (MAX_BPS - slippageToleranceBps) / MAX_BPS;
missingMitigations: `slippageToleranceBps` is owner-set with cap of MAX_BPS=10_000 → owner can set 10000 and disable slippage entirely (no `minOut`); revert never fires
No staleness/sequencer check (irrelevant here — no Chainlink — but no independent reference either)
findings.notes: WARNING in the contract NatSpec already states rebasing/yield-decreasing vaults are unsupported. The intended design is that `convertToShares` is roughly the fair AMM rate; this is a known economic assumption. Flag for econ-scanner: scenarios where the ERC4626 vault's share price diverges from AMM (e.g. AMM depeg of vault token, withdrawal queue / cooldown distortions like sUSDe) would let a flash-trader execute the swap at the unfavourable end of the tolerance band. The owner-only MAX_BPS=10_000 ceiling on `slippageToleranceBps` is a centralization knob, not a security boundary.

findings.description: Both helpers loop over `clients.length` (the full `_authorizedClients.values()` set). Each iteration in `_accrueSurplusShares` performs at least one external `vault.convertToShares` call and a SLOAD on `setAsideBufferSize[client]`. `_distributeBuffer` additionally performs one `safeTransfer` per buffered client. With a sufficiently large authorized-client set, the single `skimSurplus` call risks exceeding the block gas limit.
missingMitigations: No explicit cap on the authorized-client set size
findings.notes: The set is owner-controlled, so realistic abuse requires malicious/incompetent owner. Per known-issues policy (reckless admin mistakes are out of scope) this is QA at best. Included so econ-scanner can decide whether story-042 changed the gas profile materially.

findings.description: `totalShares` is the SUM of per-client `vault.convertToShares(surplus_i)` (each independently floored). Sum-of-floors is always <= floor-of-sum, so `totalShares <= vault.convertToShares(aggregateSurplus)` is a tautology, making the loud aggregate-surplus require (line 429) effectively defense-in-depth and never a real bound. The `minOut` is then computed on this under-counted `totalShares`, yielding a marginally SMALLER `minOut` than the protocol's fair-share would imply — slightly weakening slippage protection. The drift is bounded by `clients.length` wei in shares (one wei rounding per client).
missingMitigations: No single-shot `convertToShares(aggregateSurplus)` used as the swap basis (the contract chooses per-client floors deliberately per the 'protocol-favoring rounding' comment)
findings.notes: Author's comment explicitly calls the protocol-favoring rounding intentional. The minOut weakening is dust-scale unless `clients.length` is large AND the vault's `convertToShares` has wide rounding error. Forwarded for econ-scanner to confirm the slippage degradation stays within the documented `slippageToleranceBps` envelope and is not exploitable as a sandwich-with-many-clients amplifier.

skipped.reason: deposit gated by onlyAuthorizedClient; this strategy buys vault tokens via AMM and tracks principal in clientBalances, not minted shares; not an open vault.
No special branch for totalSupply()==0; clientBalances accounting is per-client principal.
No Chainlink usage. ERC4626 spot conversion is used but is not an oracle in the Chainlink sense (separate pattern PATTERN-002 covers it).

nonReentrant on every external entry point; principal accounting is intentionally untouched during skim so cross-call state coherence is preserved; underlying is configured per-deployment (not user-supplied).
No ecrecover / EIP-712 paths in scope.
safeIncreaseAllowance / forceApprove used; C4 known-invalid finding category.
Folded into PATTERN-002 (AMM-vs-vault price divergence is the real surface; classic getReserves()/slot0() pattern not present).

Owner-set buffers and slippage are gated by Ownable; per C4 policy this is QA/known-issue. setAsideBufferSize being writable for not-yet-authorized client addresses is a stale-state surface, not a security bug — the buffer only applies when that address is in _authorizedClients.
SafeERC20 throughout; swap return value captured.
Boundary operators audited (e.g. `totalValue > td`, `totalShares <= convertToShares(aggregateSurplus)`, `amount > availablePrincipal`) all use the protocol-favoring direction.
Two-phase totalWithdrawal has explicit WAITING_PERIOD/EXECUTION_WINDOW enforcement; emergencyWithdraw is owner-only by design and out-of-scope as 'reckless admin'.
